sections.description: A self-hosted conversational site search for WordPress. No external APIs are used for search, and visitor queries never leave your server. Field-weighted BM25 ranking with intent matching, exact phrase search, synonym expansion, and optional PDF and image indexing.
sections.changelog:
0.9.21 — finishing the asset extraction

Ten low-severity findings from an external re-test of 0.9.20. Nothing about indexing, ranking, the visitor path or the schema changes, so no reindex is required.

  • Changed: a multi-result answer opens at its first result. The widget scrolled to the bottom of the message log after every reply — right for a short answer, wrong for one taller than the panel, where the visitor arrived at the last result with the first and its framing message scrolled off the top. A reply that does not fit now opens at its own top instead. Short replies still scroll to the bottom as before.
  • Fixed: feedback recording was not atomic. The endpoint read the rating column, checked it was still NULL and then wrote it, with nothing holding the row in between — so two submissions arriving together could both pass the check and the second overwrite the first. That is the one-rating-per-answer rule of 0.9.7 failing at exactly the moment it applies. The window is small and the prize is changing your own rating, so this is an integrity fault rather than a vulnerability, but the write now carries AND feedback IS NULL in its WHERE clause and the database decides which request arrived first. The loser gets a 409, which the widget already treats as success.
  • Fixed: the documentation said the inline-asset extraction was finished, and four blocks remained. 0.9.20 moved the Diagnostics CSS and JavaScript into real files and then stated in five separate places that the work was complete — while the intents, synonyms and Appearance screens still carried 417 lines of inline CSS and script between them, rather more than had actually been extracted. The cost falls on anyone who read that and set a strict admin Content-Security-Policy: the Appearance screen’s live preview would have gone silently dead and three screens unstyled, having been told the opposite. The extraction is now genuinely complete — the three remaining <style> blocks are in assets/css/mbr-isa-admin.css and the Appearance script is in a new assets/js/mbr-isa-appearance.js, with its preset list and glass bounds passed through wp_localize_script().
  • Fixed: the translation template had not been regenerated since 0.9.10. The 0.9.8 audit found that no .pot shipped at all; that was fixed in 0.9.10 and has been quietly regressing ever since, leaving every string added across ten releases untranslatable. The visible casualty was the new tab strip — only Status and Feedback existed as msgids, so a translated site showed two translated tabs and five English ones. Regenerated: 325 strings, current line references.
  • Fixed: the reindex button pointed at controls that had moved. The Status tab described itself as indexing “the post types selected below”; the tab split put those checkboxes on the Content tab.
  • Fixed: the PDF extractor collapsed whitespace twice. Two identical passes three lines apart, the first redundant over the full text of every PDF and the second strictly better, having the byte-wise fallback the first lacked. Predates 0.9.20.
  • Fixed: a stylesheet rule that matched nothing. [id^="mbr-isa-synonym-"] was added in 0.9.20 but the synonyms screen uses that string as a class, not an id. Rather than drop the selector, the synonyms screen now has the same anchored-save behaviour the intents screen gained in 0.9.20 — saving returns you to the card you were working on — which makes the rule true.
  • Fixed: four dead global $wpdb; declarations left by the tab split, in renderers that do not touch the database.
  • Changed: class-mbr-isa-frontend.php was the only tab-indented file in the tree and now uses four spaces like the other twenty. Whitespace only.

0.9.20 — a tabbed Diagnostics screen

An admin usability release. Nothing about indexing, ranking or the visitor path changes, so no reindex is required and the schema is unchanged at v6.

  • The Diagnostics screen is now tabbed. It had grown a section at a time into one long scroll of unrelated controls, which made the panel you wanted hard to find and the one you did not want easy to change on the way past. There are now seven tabs — Status, Content, Alt Text, Privacy, Widget, Feedback and Testers. Each renders on its own rather than being hidden with CSS, so only the active tab’s queries run: the feedback statistics aggregate the query log and the alt text worklist reads up to 4,000 published posts, and until now both ran every time the screen was opened. Saving any setting returns you to the tab that owns it.
  • Adding an intent no longer throws you back to the top of the page. Saving redirected to the top of the intents screen, so adding several in a row meant scrolling to the bottom again each time. A save now returns to the card it concerns: the blank add form after an addition, ready for the next one, or the edited intent’s own card otherwise. Validation errors deliberately keep you at the top, because that is where the notice explaining the failure is.
  • Admin CSS and JavaScript are no longer inline. They now ship as assets/css/mbr-isa-admin.css and assets/js/mbr-isa-admin.js, with values PHP used to print into the markup passed through wp_localize_script(). Inline blocks cannot be cached and are refused by a strict admin Content-Security-Policy, and there were seven across five screens — a cost that rose with every new panel. This was the outstanding finding from the 0.9.18 re-test. Clear any admin asset cache after upgrading.
  • The four $_GET display flags on the Diagnostics screen now go through wp_unslash() and sanitize_key(), closing the part of the superglobal finding that 0.9.19 left partially fixed.

0.9.19 — re-test fixes

No reindex required, and no schema change. Six low-severity findings from an external re-test of 0.9.18, all in code added between 0.9.9 and 0.9.18.

  • Fixed: a PDF whose text was invalid UTF-8 still lost all of it. The fallback for a failed unicode scrub ran against a variable the failure had already emptied, so the retry scrubbed an empty string and the document was reported as having no text layer — indistinguishable from a genuine scan. This is the same defect corrected elsewhere in the same function in 0.9.9, with one of the two instances missed at the time.
  • Fixed: the tokeniser decoded HTML entities twice. Two identical html_entity_decode() calls sat three lines apart, so double-encoded content was decoded back into markup in the stored passage — an escaped code sample reading &lt;script&gt; was indexed as a literal <script>. Never exploitable through the plugin, since snippets are escaped before highlighting and the admin screens escape too, but it turned inert text into markup-shaped text in a field the public REST response carried.
  • Fixed: intent_supplementary_max could not return more than one result. The supplementary path reuses the full formatting path and inherited its confidence cap; at high confidence result_limit_high is 1, so the caller's maximum of three was unreachable. The better the supplementary hits scored, the fewer were shown — exactly the case the setting exists for. The maximum is now passed in rather than applied to what comes back.
  • Fixed: the contents-page demotion fetched every contents row in the index. The 0.9.9 index stopped this being a full table scan but left it unbounded in rows returned, while the loop beneath can only demote documents the query already matched. The query is now scoped to the matched set.
  • Changed: mbstring is declared as a requirement rather than half-guarded. Six scattered function_exists() guards promised a graceful degradation the rest of the code could not deliver — the indexer, responder and tokeniser all call mb_* unconditionally, so without the extension the plugin fatalled regardless. They also cost a lookup per token of every document. There is now a runtime check beside the PHP version guard, with an admin notice.
  • Changed: the full stored passage is no longer sent to every visitor. Each result carried its whole 2,000-character passage in excerpt alongside the 240-character snippet the widget renders — roughly 6 KB of dead payload on a three-result response, on an unauthenticated endpoint. Nothing private was exposed; every row had already passed the visibility gate.
  • Credits: the passage chunker and the WP-CLI commands contain code contributed by James Wilson (Director of Technology, Cogora), who also carried out the 0.9.8 audit and this re-test.

0.9.18 — truncated documents, and further mentions

A full reindex is required.

  • Fixed: content that merely mentioned <body> was truncated. The body-only rule added in 0.9.13 ran on every field, including text extracted from a PDF, and its unclosed-tag branch discarded everything before the mention. A post whose mention fell after its prose indexed as nothing at all; the plugin's own user guide lost its first five pages and had the survivors renumbered from 1, sending PDF deep links to the wrong page. The rule now requires a doctype or an <html> tag near the start before it applies.
  • New: further mentions in the same document. Collapse gives each document one result, so a term mentioned three times in one PDF was reachable only at its best-scoring passage. The others now ride along beneath it as secondary links, each with its own snippet, deep link and — for PDFs — page number. Ranking and the confidence caps are unchanged. Capped at three; passage_extras_max 0 restores the previous behaviour.
  • Changed: high confidence now requires the runner-up to be a non-answer. The dominance test was a ratio, which a leader could satisfy while the second result was still worth showing — and high confidence returns one result, so that answer was cut. Searching a person's name made it obvious. The caps are settable through result_limit_high, result_limit_medium and result_limit_low, clamped 1–10.
  • Fixed: a mention's page label could name the wrong page. A passage records the page it starts on and a chunk routinely runs onto the next, so a match in its later half sits a page further on. The deep link corrected for that; the label did not.
  • Fixed: Decorative did not stick in the Alt Text Audit. It stored empty alt text, which the scan cannot tell apart from alt text nobody wrote, so the image returned to the worklist on every scan. A marker now records the decision; the alt attribute is still written empty.
  • Fixed: WooCommerce product galleries reported as unused. A gallery is stored as a bare comma-separated ID list that no markup or JSON pattern matches, so live product images sank to the bottom of the worklist. Plain ID-list meta is now read, filterable through mbr_isa_id_list_meta_keys.

0.9.17 — page-builder references

A full reindex is required.

  • Fixed: page-builder layouts were invisible to the reference scan. Builders store layouts as JSON, and JSON escapes forward slashes — so a stored path such as 2025/12/photo.png sits in the meta as 2025\/12\/photo.png and could never match. This affected every attachment on every Elementor- or Bricks-built site, PDFs as well as images.
  • Elementor's thumbnail cache compounded it, serving images from a path containing only the filename stem and a hash, in which the original path appears nowhere at all.
  • A last-resort pass now matches on the filename stem and proves the match in PHP rather than trusting a substring, requiring a path boundary followed by the file's own extension or a recognised derivative suffix.
  • The verification is what makes this safe. A bare substring search would read a separate upload called logo-2.png as a reference to logo.png, wrongly treating an unpublished image as published — loosening a visibility rule, which this scan must never do.

0.9.16 — featured images count as published usage

A full reindex is required.

  • Fixed: a featured image was invisible to the visibility scan. Whether an attachment counts as published is decided by looking for its stored file path in post content and post meta. A featured image appears in neither — it is recorded as _thumbnail_id holding the attachment's ID, and the theme renders it from there.
  • Such an image was indexed only if its post_parent happened to be readable, and that parent then became the URL the result linked to — so a blog post's featured image could be indexed under, and link to, an unrelated page.
  • Featured images are now checked first, before the content and meta scans: an exact match on an indexed meta key, materially cheaper than the LIKE scans it precedes.
  • Expect the indexed image count to rise after reindexing.

0.9.15 — image results linked to the wrong page

No schema change; a reindex is not required.

  • Fixed: an image result could link to a page the image does not appear on. The result URL preferred the attachment's post_parent, which records which editor a file was uploaded from — not which page displays it. Dragging a photo into a page once, even into a block later deleted, sets that page as the parent permanently, so an image used on a blog post could send the visitor to the About page instead.
  • Image results now prefer a post that actually references the file, falling back to the parent only when nothing does. This reverses the PDF ordering deliberately: a PDF's parent is nearly always the page offering the download, whereas an image's parent is usually an upload artefact.
  • The choice is now deterministic. Candidates are sorted after fetching — most recent first, then descending ID — so an image appearing on several posts no longer links somewhere different on each request.

0.9.14 — deep link regression

A full reindex is required.

  • Fixed: deep links stopped scrolling to and highlighting the matched passage. The bounded tag remover added in 0.9.13 replaced every remaining tag with a space, where strip_tags() had replaced it with nothing. Block-level tags are converted to markers earlier, so everything reaching that step is inline — and those sit inside a sentence. “Uses <strong>WordPress</strong>’s own” was indexed as “Uses WordPress ’s own”.
  • Deep links use the Text Fragments standard, which requires the quoted run to match the rendered page exactly. A fabricated space means the browser cannot find the passage, so it loads the page and silently declines to scroll.
  • Quoted phrase search across inline markup failed the same way, as did snippet accuracy wherever a link or bold run sat mid-sentence.

0.9.13 — silent content loss during indexing

A full reindex is required.

  • Fixed: one malformed tag could cost a page its entire content. The indexer used strip_tags() for its final HTML removal, and strip_tags() has no upper bound on how far it searches for a closing bracket. A single unterminated construct consumed everything after it — on a real 36,965-character page, 47 characters reached the index: the contents of <title> and nothing else.
  • The failure was silent. The page rendered perfectly and appeared in the document count while returning nothing for any word in its body. Quoted phrase search was merely where it became visible.
  • Tag removal is now bounded: a run counts as a tag only when it begins with a name character and closes within a plausible distance, so a malformation costs its own fragment rather than the rest of the page.
  • Added: a full HTML document in post_content is indexed on its <body> only. On the same page, 21,641 of 36,913 characters were head — inline CSS and meta tags being fed to the chunker as prose.
  • Affected pages hold a near-empty row each until the index is rebuilt. Expect the document count to hold steady while chunks, terms and postings rise.

0.9.12 — HTML entities in the index

A full reindex is required. Fixes a fault present since the tokeniser landed, affecting quoted phrase search, the term dictionary, and snippets shown to visitors.

  • Fixed: HTML entities were never decoded during indexing. WordPress stores an ampersand in post content as & and a curly apostrophe as ’. The indexer stripped tags but never decoded them, so a heading reading “Rules & Targeting” was stored as Rules & Targeting.
  • Quoted phrase search failed on any phrase containing such a character. Searching for the phrase compared it against a stored passage still holding the encoded form and returned nothing found, on a page where the words were plainly visible. Apostrophes failed identically.
  • The term dictionary was polluted. With the entity left encoded, the tokeniser stripped the punctuation around it and indexed the remnant as a word: & became the term “amp”, ’ became “8217”,   became “nbsp” — real searchable entries attached to a large fraction of a typical site's pages.
  • Snippets shown to visitors contained raw entities, so any passage with an ampersand displayed as literal & in the chat panel.
  • Entities are decoded after tags are stripped, never before — decoding first would turn an encoded <script> back into a real tag, whereas decoding afterwards leaves inert literal text that is escaped again at render time.
  • Decoding is applied when comparing a quoted phrase as well as at indexing time, so quoted search starts working the moment the files are in place. The dictionary and stored snippets still need the reindex.

0.9.11 — documentation accuracy

No schema change, no reindex, no front-end behaviour change.

  • Fixed: wp mbr-isa status did not report image indexing. The 0.9.10 user guide documented an Image indexing: line the command never printed — the CLI was overlooked when image support was added in 0.9.9. It now reports the on/off state together with the number of images actually in the index.
  • The count is included because an image has two independent ways to be excluded, the visibility rule and the alt text requirement, so “on” with a count of zero is a real and fairly common state meaning the setting is enabled but nothing qualifies. Reporting the switch alone would leave that looking like a failed reindex.
  • Every other filter, setting, option and cron hook documented in the 0.9.10 guide has been re-checked against the source. This was the only discrepancy.

0.9.10 — alt text audit

No schema change and no reindex needed. Adds a tool for finding and fixing images with no alt text, which is also what makes image indexing worth switching on.

  • Added: an Alt Text Audit panel on the Diagnostics screen. It lists images with no alt text, ranked by how many published pages actually display each one. A logo used on forty pages and a cropped duplicate nobody ever used are both “missing alt text”, and an alphabetical list of three hundred files gives no way to tell them apart — sorted this way, the top twenty rows are most of the value.
  • Alt text is written straight from the table. Each row carries a thumbnail, the filename, any existing caption or description, where the image is used and a link to the page it appears on — enough to write the sentence without opening anything else. Enter saves, so a long list can be worked through from the keyboard, and an image that becomes eligible is reindexed on the spot rather than at the next full reindex.
  • A Decorative action stores empty alt text deliberately, which is the correct answer for spacers, flourishes and borders and tells a screen reader to skip the image.
  • It does not write alt text for you, and that is deliberate. The plugin cannot see images. Anything it generated would be inferred from the filename or the surrounding page, which is not a description of the picture — and alt text describing the wrong thing is worse for a screen reader user than none at all. Only somebody looking at the image can tell a decorative flourish from a photograph carrying meaning. The panel ranks the work and supplies the context; a person writes the words.
  • The usage scan reads page-builder layouts as well as post content. Elementor and Bricks keep their layouts as JSON in post meta rather than in post_content, so a scan reading only post content would report almost every image on such a site as unused and invert the entire ranking. Filterable through mbr_isa_builder_meta_keys.
  • The scan is inverted rather than per-image: one pass over published content builds usage counts for every image at once, so its cost scales with the number of posts rather than with the size of the Media Library, and there is no per-file LIKE scan anywhere in it.
  • Editing alt text requires edit_post on the attachment itself rather than manage_options, so an editor who can already do this in the Media Library can use the panel, and nobody reaches an attachment they could not otherwise edit.

0.9.9 — image indexing, and an external audit

Schema v6 — additive, applied automatically on upgrade. A full reindex is needed before images appear in results; the audit fixes need none. Nine medium and nineteen low-severity findings from an external security and code audit of 0.9.8 are resolved here; no critical or high-severity issue was identified.

  • Added: image indexing, off by default. Images are indexed on their alt text, caption, description and filename — everything a person has written about the picture. Nothing is read from the image itself. JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and AVIF; SVG is deliberately excluded.
  • Alt text is the primary signal and, by default, required. It is the one field written specifically to describe what is in a picture, so images that have it are indexed and the rest are skipped. The requirement can be switched off, at which point a caption, a description or an informative filename will do instead. Either way it is re-tested at search time, so deleting an image's alt text removes it from results without waiting for a reindex.
  • Filenames are cleaned before indexing and uninformative ones ignored entirely. Extensions, WordPress's generated size suffixes, -scaled and image-editor suffixes are stripped, so jpg and png never become search terms matching every image on the site. Camera and screenshot defaults — IMG_4821, DSC00042, Screenshot-2026-08-18-at-09.41.22, hex blobs from media managers — are recognised and skipped, since indexing them puts high-frequency junk into the dictionary that can only ever produce a wrong answer.
  • An image result links to the page the image appears on, not to the file. Sending a visitor to a bare .jpg is technically the resource that matched and a dead end as an answer. Adjustable through mbr_isa_image_result_url.
  • Results carry a thumbnail and an IMAGE badge, and clicking the thumbnail opens the picture in a lightbox rather than following the link. The lightbox traps focus, closes on Escape or a click outside, restores focus where it came from, and shows the alt text with a link through to the page. It remains a real link to the file underneath, so middle-click and open-in-new-tab behave normally.
  • Corrected a scoring fault images would otherwise have caused. BM25 normalises by document length, and an image row holds five to ten tokens against a corpus average dominated by PDF passage chunks running to several hundred — so an image would have taken roughly a 45% scoring advantage over the page it sits on, for no reason beyond being short. Image rows are floored to the corpus average for each field, the point at which normalisation is exactly neutral, so an image competes on whether its words match rather than on how few of them there are. Further tunable through mbr_isa_image_score_weight.
  • Which images qualify is a separate setting from which PDFs do, using the same three modes. They look alike and mean very different things: “every PDF in the Media Library” is a hundred documents somebody deliberately produced, while “every image” is several thousand files including every cropped duplicate and abandoned upload.
  • Fixed (audit): feedback ratings were rejected outright on every site with a negative UTC offset. Query rows are written in site-local time but the expiry check compared them against a UTC clock, so a row appeared more than an hour old the moment it was created and every rating returned 410. On a positive offset the same fault silently extended the window instead.
  • Fixed (audit): an undefined variable on the public search path. pages_before_match() referred to a $phrase its signature never declared, emitting a PHP warning for every PDF result whose passage crossed a page boundary. With display_errors on, that warning was written ahead of the REST response — corrupting the JSON and disclosing the plugin's absolute path. Quoted searches on PDFs also opened at the wrong page.
  • Fixed (audit): an undefined array key on every shortcode render, with the same warning-in-the-body consequence.
  • Fixed (audit): a malformed PDF could hang the request that uploaded it. Neither the depth limit nor the page-count limit bounded a cyclic page tree, since a node whose children point back at it branches two ways per level and adds nothing to the page list on the way. Any user able to upload a file could trigger it.
  • Fixed (audit): a PDF whose text survived extraction as invalid UTF-8 lost all of it. The fallback for a failed unicode whitespace pass ran against an empty string rather than the extracted text, so the document was reported as having no text layer instead of indexing partially.
  • Fixed (audit): the Diagnostics screen could take itself down on the sites that most needed it. The PDF eligibility figure tested up to 500 files, each costing two unindexable LIKE scans, in one page load. Both the PDF and image figures now test a bounded sample and say so.
  • Fixed (audit): every visitor search full-scanned the documents table looking for contents pages — the last unbounded query on the visitor path. Resolved with an index.
  • Fixed (audit): orphan-term pruning ran on every post save, trash and delete, a full anti-join across the terms and postings tables. It bought nothing, since a term with no postings is invisible to search; it now runs only where the index is already being walked.
  • Changed (audit): the /ask endpoint declares a length bound at the route, so an oversized body is rejected before wp_strip_all_tags() runs over all of it.
  • Changed (audit): the session identifier is stored on a visitor's device only when query logging is on. PECR regulation 6 covers all storage on terminal equipment, not only cookies, and the identifier serves the query log rather than the delivery of the search.
  • Added (audit): languages/mbr-isa.pot. load_plugin_textdomain() pointed at a directory that did not exist, so every translatable string was permanently inert. Fixing it also closed a related fault, where the wp_kses() allowlist on one admin string permitted an onclick attribute a malicious translation could have used.
  • Changed (audit): the update check no longer transmits the site's PHP version, locale and installed plugin version to GitHub. The manifest is a static file that ignores them.
  • Fixed (audit): uninstalling a network-activated copy now cleans every site in the network rather than only the current one.
  • Added (audit): the Update URI: header, so a WordPress.org plugin claiming this slug cannot serve an update to this one.
  • Housekeeping (audit): feedback statistics and query-log retention no longer mix the database server's clock with WordPress's site-local time, constructor parameters use explicit nullable types (implicit nullability is deprecated in PHP 8.4), and a \u2014 escape in a single-quoted string no longer prints literally in WP-CLI.

0.9.8 — code-review follow-up

No schema change and no reindex needed. Two fixes: the last place where the plugin held a second, looser definition of "public", and a cosmetic fault that has been possible on every version.

  • Fixed: the PDF reference scan did not apply the new access-control filter. Whether a published post mentions a file's path is a question SQL can answer; whether that post is publicly readable is not, because mbr_isa_can_index_post is arbitrary PHP and cannot be expressed as a WHERE clause. A members-only page correctly kept out of the index by the filter therefore still counted as evidence that a PDF it links to was published, and the file's full text was indexed and served to anonymous visitors — the same access-control gap 0.9.7 closed, one level down in the PDF subsystem.
  • Candidate posts are now retrieved and re-tested through the same central visibility check, in the post-content and post-meta passes alike, so post indexing, search-time revalidation, PDF parents and PDF references all ask one question of one function. Candidates are capped and the batch is primed in a single query; overrunning the cap fails closed, costing a search result rather than disclosing one. The new mbr_isa_pdf_reference_candidates filter raises the cap on sites where files are linked from very many places.
  • Fixed: a stripe of panel background between the input row and the credit line. The stylesheet never reset the <form> element's own margin, so a host theme styling forms with a bottom margin opened a gap between two blocks that share the same background. Long-standing rather than new, and dependent entirely on the theme. The panel's four sections and the two controls inside the form row now zero their margins, scoped deeply enough to outrank a theme rule aimed at forms inside the content wrapper.
  • A stale-index purge is scheduled after upgrading, as in 0.9.7. An index built by 0.9.7 may hold PDF rows the corrected reference rule no longer admits; nothing stale can be served in any case, since every result is re-tested against today's rules before it is returned, so this is housekeeping rather than a security control.

0.9.7 — security, scalability, and contents-page detection

No schema change. None of the security work below needs a reindex — every result is re-checked as it is returned, so an index built by any earlier version is safe to carry forward. The contents-page fix is applied while indexing, so run a full reindex when convenient to have it reach documents already stored.

  • Fixed (important): published and unprotected was not a sufficient test of public. A membership or paywall plugin routinely leaves a post with the status publish and no password while refusing the content to anonymous visitors, and nothing in the post row records that. A post's type must now also be viewable on the front end, and the new mbr_isa_can_index_post filter lets a plugin that does know about a restriction declare it. The filter is deny-only: it runs after the built-in conditions and cannot unlock a draft or a protected post.
  • Added: every result is re-checked against the live post before it is returned. The index is a cache of a decision taken at index time, and a cache goes stale — through an access-control plugin, an upgrade from narrower rules, a post type re-registered as private, or a rule change that cannot retract what earlier rules wrote. A row whose source has since become private, protected, restricted or deleted is now discarded rather than served. This is a floor beneath a whole class of stale-index disclosure rather than a fix for one leak.
  • Fixed: the indexer trusted the settings screen for a security decision. Content Sources deliberately keeps a post type ticked while the plugin registering it is deactivated, so a temporary deactivation cannot silently drop content from your configuration. That is right for a settings list and wrong as a foundation for visibility, so the indexer now verifies post-type viewability itself.
  • Fixed: a PDF counted as published if anything at all linked to it. The reference test excluded revisions and attachments and admitted every other post type, including reusable blocks, page-builder templates and private custom post types — things with no front end. A link is only evidence of publication if the page doing the linking is itself reachable, so the test now names the types that qualify.
  • Fixed: contents-page detection never fired on documents whose entries carry no full stop. The test looked for “3. How it works”; a great many documents write “3 How it works” instead, this plugin's own user guide among them. Such a page registered no entries at all, so it was neither demoted nor stood aside for the chapter it lists. Both forms are recognised now, the dotless one requiring a capital after the number so that a data table reading “30 requests per minute” does not qualify.
  • Fixed alongside it: the run of entries is measured on its own rather than averaged across the whole passage. A short contents list sharing a chunk with ordinary prose is still the densest list of topics in the document, but the prose either side of it lifted the average and let it through. Decimals remain excluded, so settings reference tables are unaffected.
  • Improved: search no longer measures the whole index on every query. Field lengths were derived from an aggregate across the entire postings table for every visitor question — affordable on a small site, an architectural problem on a large one. Only documents containing a query term are loaded now, and corpus statistics are cached until an index write invalidates them. Scores, confidence levels and result ordering are unchanged.
  • Changed: one feedback rating per answer. A token stays valid for an hour and was not consumed by use, so a caller holding one could resubmit repeatedly and move the statistics. A second submission returns 409, checked after the token rather than before it, since whether a query has been rated is itself information. A rating whose response was lost in transit now reports success rather than failure on retry.
  • Added: update packages are verified against a checksum published in this manifest. The update path is a code-delivery path resting on two hosts, and WordPress verifies nothing it did not fetch from WordPress.org. Where the manifest carries a checksum, the downloaded package is checked against it before anything is unpacked. Backward compatible — a manifest without one updates as before — and MBR_ISA_REQUIRE_SIGNED_UPDATES makes verification mandatory.
  • Added: wp mbr-isa purge, with --dry-run, to remove indexed rows whose source no longer passes the visibility rules. Housekeeping rather than a security control, since nothing stale can be served in any case. A background pass runs after upgrading; a full reindex does the same job.
  • Improved: a full reindex asks the host for more execution time and memory before starting. WP-CLI remains the reliable route on large sites.

0.9.6 — a contents page no longer hides its own chapter

  • Fixed: a document's contents page could make the chapter it lists unreachable. Results collapse to one passage per document, so when a contents page outranked the chapter it named, it did not appear alongside that chapter — it replaced it. The document's single result was a list of headings, and no rephrasing would reach the prose behind them.
  • This was self-defeating for exactly the query it was meant to serve. Contents passages are demoted rather than excluded so that someone searching a section title can still find it — yet searching a chapter title landed on the contents-page line naming that chapter, not on the chapter.
  • Where a document has any matching passage that is not a contents page, that passage now represents it. A contents chunk is used only when nothing else in the same document matched — what the demotion was always trying to express, applied within a document rather than across the index.
  • Nothing is lost: a search matching only a contents page still returns it. A document's position now follows the score of whichever passage represents it, so a substitution can move it down the list — correct, since the score reflects what the visitor will be shown.
  • contents_score_penalty is unchanged and still governs ranking between documents. Added contents_prefer_body (default true) to restore the previous behaviour.

0.9.5 — snippet accuracy, and sentence breaks in PDF snippets

  • Fixed: a multi-word search could open the snippet on the wrong occurrence. The snippet opened at the first occurrence of any query term rather than where the terms appeared together, so a passage mentioning one of your words in its opening line opened there — leaving the phrase you actually wanted further down, in the next snippet.
  • Each occurrence is now scored by how many distinct query terms fall within a window around it, and the densest wins. Ties go to prose over code, then to the earliest position, so single-term queries behave exactly as before.
  • The snippet builder and the deep-link builder share this helper, so PDF results now also open at the page where the terms actually cluster.
  • Added: sentence breaks in PDF snippets. PDFs carry no block structure, so their snippets arrived as one unbroken run. Sentence boundaries now stand in for paragraphs — artificial, but a three-sentence snippet is markedly easier to scan.
  • The guards matter more than the rule, since technical prose is full of full stops that end nothing. Section references such as § 11.5., version numbers, initials as in "R. Palmer", and abbreviations including e.g., i.e., etc., Fig. and Ltd. are all left alone. Very short fragments stay attached rather than stranded on a line of their own.
  • Posts and pages are unchanged — they carry real block structure and already break on it.

0.9.4 — PDF link zoom, and paragraph breaks in snippets

A reindex is required if you installed 0.9.2 or 0.9.3.

  • Fixed: a positioned PDF link zoomed the document to fit the window. Scrolling used the view=FitH open parameter, which also fits the page to the window width — on a normal desktop, opening at around 163% instead of 100%. Links now use zoom=scale,left,top, which states the scale explicitly. It defaults to 100% and is configurable through pdf_link_zoom.
  • Any open parameter that scrolls must also set a view, so a scale has to be named — there is no way to say "scroll here and leave the zoom alone".
  • The two parameters use opposite origins: view=FitH measures up from the bottom-left in PDF user space, zoom measures down from the top-left. The stored offset changed to match, so an index built by 0.9.2 holds the mirror image and must be rebuilt.
  • Added: snippets now show paragraph breaks. Block boundaries in post content were flattened to spaces, running two paragraphs together as one sentence. They render as line breaks now, which makes a multi-paragraph snippet considerably easier to read.
  • Posts and pages only. A PDF's line breaks are hard wraps from the original layout — a break every dozen words, mid sentence — so reproducing them would make snippets more ragged rather than more readable, and they were collapsed before storage in any case. A page boundary inside a PDF passage stays a space: a page break is a layout event, not a change of thought.
  • <br> joins <mark> as the only markup the responder introduces, added after escaping so it cannot originate in the source text.

0.9.3 — fixes a fatal error in 0.9.2

  • Fixed: fatal error on any site upgrading to 0.9.2. The schema migration for the new page_top column called a helper on $this from inside a static method, so every admin page load ended in "Using $this when not in object context" as soon as the plugin bootstrapped. The migration runs on plugins_loaded, so the site was down rather than merely degraded.
  • Fixed: the same migration ran before the one that adds page_number, while positioning itself AFTER page_number. On a site coming from schema 3 that column would not yet exist, the ALTER would fail, and schema 5 would be recorded with the column missing. The steps are now in version order.
  • 0.9.2 was withdrawn. Its feature — PDF links that land on the passage rather than the top of the page — is unchanged and described in the 0.9.2 entry below. A full reindex is still required.

0.9.2 — PDF links land on the passage

Schema v5. Run a full reindex after updating, or PDF links keep their old behaviour.

  • Added: PDF results now open near the matching passage rather than at the top of the page. A link has always used #page=N, which scrolls the top of that page into view — so a passage halfway down the page left the visitor a screen above it, and on a dense page that meant most of a page of hunting. Links now carry a vertical target as well, via the view=FitH open parameter.
  • How the position is derived: the extractor reads the operators that move the text cursor but discards their operands, so no coordinates exist anywhere in the index. The offset is estimated instead from how far through a page's words the passage begins, combined with the page height read from its MediaBox — new in this release. It assumes text is spread evenly down the page.
  • That assumption fails on pages with figures, tables or short closing paragraphs, so the estimate is biased upward by about a fifth of a page. The passage lands at or below the top of the view, never above it: the visitor scrolls down a little, the same direction as before but far less far.
  • Pages rotated 90 or 270 degrees are measured on their rotated height, and a MediaBox inherited from the page tree is followed. Where a height cannot be resolved for every page, no offsets are stored and links behave exactly as they did before.
  • Added: pdf_link_position (default true) to switch the behaviour off. view=FitH forces a fit-width zoom, which the open-parameter syntax gives no way to avoid, so some sites may prefer the plain page link.
  • The new column defaults to zero, meaning "no offset", so existing rows keep the old behaviour until rebuilt. Nothing breaks in the meantime — the improvement simply does not appear until you reindex.

0.9.1 — exact phrase search, and results alongside intents

  • Added: quoted phrase search. Wrapping a query in quotes — "opening hours" — searches for that exact run of words rather than the words separately. Straight and curly quotes both work, single and double.
  • A quoted query skips intent matching, so a phrase that happens to share a word with an intent trigger no longer gets the canned answer instead of the search. Synonym expansion is skipped too, since swapping in different words is the opposite of what an exact search asks for.
  • How it works: the index holds no positional data, so the stems find candidate passages and each candidate's stored passage text is then checked for the literal phrase. The check runs before chunks are collapsed to one row per document, so a phrase in a document's third chunk is still found when its first chunk scores higher.
  • Phrase matching ignores case and treats any run of whitespace as a single space, so a phrase still matches across a line break in a PDF. Titles are searched as well as passage text, and curly quotes and non-breaking spaces inside the phrase are folded before comparison.
  • Limitation: a phrase is only found if it survives whole inside one passage chunk. The 50-word overlap between chunks makes this rare, but a very long phrase spanning a boundary can be missed. When nothing matches, the reply names the phrase and suggests searching without the quotes.
  • Added: search results can appear beneath an intent answer. Where a query matches an intent and also produces good search hits, those hits are offered under the canned response instead of being discarded. Controlled by intent_supplementary_results (on by default) and intent_supplementary_max (default 3).
  • Only medium-confidence-or-better hits are shown. An intent has already answered the question, so padding it with weak matches would make a confident answer read as hedging.
  • Fixed while building the above: phrase detection used substr() where mbstring is unavailable, which works in bytes — the first byte of a curly quote never matched the three-byte character, so smart-quoted phrases fell through to an ordinary search on precisely the mobile keyboards most likely to produce them. Detection now uses a unicode-safe regular expression needing only PCRE.

0.9.0 — documentation audit

No behaviour changes. Every factual claim in the user guide was checked against the source; seven were wrong or incomplete. The plugin code is unchanged apart from the version constant.

  • Corrected: the widget is skipped on feeds, embeds and robots.txt — not on the favicon endpoint, which the documentation claimed and the code never checked.
  • Corrected: the chunk-overlap cap. The quarter-size fallback applies only when the overlap is greater than or equal to the chunk size, so an excessive-but-smaller value such as 200 on a 250-word chunk is accepted as given and will bloat the index.
  • Corrected: the query log also stores the normalised token list and the top result's document ID, and truncates query text to 500 characters. The privacy section now lists everything the table holds.
  • Documented: /ask silently truncates queries to 500 characters rather than rejecting longer input.
  • Documented: the feedback endpoint returns { "ok": true } on success.
  • Documented: the mbr_isa_stopwords filter, which has existed since the tokeniser landed.
  • Documented: nine settings keys are absent from the options row until set, with the default applied in code rather than seeded on activation.
  • Documented: the shipped intents and synonym groups apply whenever the stored list is empty, not only on first install — deleting your last intent restores all five defaults.

0.8.8 — audit follow-up

  • Changed: the plugin description no longer claims that nothing leaves your server. Search data does stay local, but the bundled update checker contacts GitHub for the manifest and littlewebshack.com for the package. The wording is now "no external APIs are used for search, and visitor queries never leave your server" — accurate, and a stronger claim besides.
  • Added: limits on regex intent triggers. At most 10 per intent, 250 characters each, and patterns nesting one repetition inside another — (a+)+, (\s*)*, (a|a)+ — are rejected on save with an explanation. Such patterns are valid but can take exponentially long to fail, and intent matching runs on the public endpoint, so a hang would be visitor-facing.
  • Ordinary triggers are unaffected: the shipped re:\bhours?\b default and patterns such as ^(contact|email) all pass.

0.8.7 — cached sites: every query failed for logged-out visitors

If you run a page cache, this is the important one. The widget answered "Something went wrong" to every question from visitors who were not logged in, while looking perfectly healthy to an administrator.

  • Fixed: a stale nonce broke the widget on page-cached sites. The widget sent an X-WP-Nonce header. WordPress verifies any nonce a REST request supplies, whatever the login state, and rejects the request with 403 if it fails. The nonce is printed into the page by wp_localize_script(), so a cached page carries whichever nonce was current when it was written — and nonces for logged-out visitors expire after 24 hours.
  • Changed: neither endpoint sends the nonce now. Both are public and unauthenticated by design and perform no capability check, so it authorised nothing and could only cause this failure. window.mbrAisa.nonce is still localised for custom integrations, but sending it is not advised.
  • Added: the widget logs the HTTP status to the browser console when a request fails. A 401 (REST disabled for logged-out users) and a 403 need different fixes, and the visitor-facing message is deliberately the same for both.

0.8.6 — Sunset contrast

  • Fixed: the Sunset preset failed WCAG AA contrast in four places. Its accent was too light to carry text on top of it and too light to be read as a link against the widget's own surfaces — the visitor's message bubble and send button at 2.86:1, links on the assistant's bubble at 1.90:1.
  • Changed: Sunset's accent is now #9c3412 and its link-hover colour #6d2a12, giving 6.86:1 for text on the accent and 4.57:1 for links. The base, surfaces and foreground colours are untouched, so the preset keeps its warm character with a deeper burnt-coral accent.
  • Sunset was the only preset affected; Mocha, Forest, Ocean and Slate Light already passed and are unchanged.

0.8.5 — mousewheel on smooth-scroll sites

  • Fixed: the mousewheel did nothing over the chat log on sites using Lenis, Locomotive Scroll, GSAP ScrollSmoother or similar. Those libraries bind wheel on window, call preventDefault() and drive the page by transform, disabling every nested scroller unless it opts out. The log stayed scrollable by scrollbar and keyboard, so the widget looked like it was working.
  • Changed: the widget sets the opt-out attributes those libraries look for and stops wheel events propagating out of the log. The wheel is released at the top and bottom of the conversation, so the page takes over once the log has nowhere further to scroll.
  • Added: overscroll-behavior: contain on the log, so a gesture running off the end no longer chains into the page behind the panel and pull-to-refresh does not fire over it on touch devices.

0.8.4 — glass readability

  • Fixed: with the glass effect enabled, the visitor's own message was unreadable. The glass rules replaced the bubble's solid accent background with a translucent tint but never changed the text colour that went with it, leaving the colour chosen to contrast against the solid accent. On Mocha that was 1.14:1 — invisible rather than merely poor. All five presets were affected; the light ones failed the same way inverted.
  • Changed: under glass the visitor's message takes a translucent mauve tint and the palette's normal foreground colour, so the two speakers stay visually distinct. Outside glass nothing changes.
  • Fixed: links inside a visitor's message follow the ordinary link colour under glass.

0.8.3 — PDF indexing fix

If you installed 0.8.2 with PDF indexing on, update and reindex.

  • Fixed: 0.8.2 indexed few or no PDFs. Its new visibility rule required the WordPress attachment relationship, which is only set when a file is uploaded from inside the post editor. Files added through Media > Add New or brought in by an import have no parent recorded — even after published pages link to them — so they were skipped.
  • Changed: the recommended setting is now "PDFs published somewhere on the site". A PDF qualifies when a published, unprotected post owns the file or references it in content or post meta. Post meta is included so page builders such as Elementor are handled.
  • Fixed: PDF-only search indexed nothing, because the old rule also required the parent's post type to be indexed.
  • Changed: sites on the 0.8.2 default are moved to the corrected setting automatically; a deliberate choice is left alone.
  • Added: the Content Sources screen reports how many PDFs currently qualify, and warns when none do.
  • Added: the mbr_isa_pdf_scan_postmeta filter.
  • The privacy intent of 0.8.2 is unchanged: a PDF nothing published points at is still not indexed.

0.8.2 — security and privacy release

Please read the first three items before updating: they change what the plugin indexes and retains.

  • Fixed (important): password-protected posts were indexed in full. A password-protected post keeps the status publish, and the indexer checked status alone — so the whole body of a protected post was indexed and served as search snippets to anonymous visitors. Indexing now requires a published status and an empty password.
  • Fixed (important): PDF indexing could expose files never meant to be found. Every PDF in the Media Library was indexed regardless of whether anything linked to it. A new "Which PDFs" setting defaults to indexing only PDFs attached to a published, unprotected post.
  • Action required: rebuild your index. These fixes govern what enters the index and cannot retract what an earlier version already stored. Run a full reindex after updating; an admin notice will prompt you.
  • Added: query log retention. The cleanup hook was never actually scheduled, so the log grew without limit. A daily cleanup now runs, configurable under Privacy on the Diagnostics screen (7/30/90 days or keep indefinitely). Upgrading sites are set to 90 days.
  • Fixed: PDF extraction had no bound on decompression — a small stream could expand without limit and exhaust the PHP process. Inflation is now capped per stream and budgeted per document.
  • Fixed: feedback ratings could be submitted against any recent query ID. Ratings now require a signed token issued with the answer.
  • Fixed: the rate limiter used a rolling expiry, so steady traffic well within the limit could still be throttled. Windows are now fixed to the clock.
  • Fixed: the rate limiter treated every visitor behind a proxy or CDN as one client. Forwarded headers are now used when explicitly trusted via MBR_ISA_TRUST_PROXY or the mbr_isa_trust_proxy filter.
  • Improved: atomic rate-limit counting where a persistent object cache is available.
  • Fixed: the first query of every session logged an empty session ID.
  • Changed: session IDs use random_bytes() rather than md5( uniqid() ).
  • Changed: corrected REST API documentation that described the endpoints as nonce-protected when the nonce is deliberately not an authentication boundary.

0.8.1

  • Fixed: table-of-contents leader runs (rows of dots and stranded page numbers) were extracted from PDFs as if they were text and appeared in snippets.
  • Added: contents pages are detected and demoted in ranking, so a table of contents no longer outranks the section it lists.
  • Improved: running headers and footers are removed from PDF text, cutting boilerplate that inflated term frequencies.
  • Improved: snippets prefer prose over code samples.
  • Fixed: PDF page links account for passages spanning a page boundary.

0.8.0

  • Added: passage-level chunk indexing, so a relevant passage deep inside a long document competes on equal terms with a short page.
  • Added: PDF results open at the matching page via #page=N.
  • Added: deep links to the matching passage using the Text Fragments standard.
  • Added: WP-CLI commands (wp mbr-isa reindex and wp mbr-isa status) for reindexing free of web-request time and memory limits.
  • Fixed: markup could leak into results as searchable text when a chunk boundary fell inside an HTML tag.

0.7.0

  • Added: optional PDF indexing with a pure-PHP text extractor (FlateDecode, ASCII85, ASCIIHex). No external binaries.
  • Added: "Maximum PDF size" setting (default 20 MB) to protect memory on shared hosting.
